newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end down on profit-taking.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended slightly down across the board on Thursday on profit-taking after sharp gains on Wednesday, traders said.
The most actively traded August 1997 contract ended at 23,720 yuan ($2,860) per tonne, losing 90 yuan.
It opened at 23,950 yuan, hitting an intra-day high of 23,980 and a low of 23,700.
May fell 70 to 23,480, June 40 to 23,660, July 100 to 23,720 and September 50 to 23,720.
Combined volume fell to 51,110 tonnes from 98,290.
Copper opened high but profit-taking pushed prices steadily down with most contracts closing near their intraday lows, traders said.
Traders said many investors were taking a wary attitude despite overnight gains on the London Metal Exchange.
"Profit-taking was responsible for today's falls," a trader said. "Most investors took a cautious approach, prefering to take profits rather than wait for possible further gains."
"Some investors are unsure of the short-term market trend despite the fact that LME copper breached the key $2,350 resistance level," a second trader said.
Despite Thursday's falls, traders said market sentiment in Shanghai had improved considerably due to heavy gains on the London Metal Exchange over the past two days.
"Improved market sentiment is likely to push copper prices through the 24,000-yuan level in the next few days despite today's falls," a third trader said.
"Shanghai copper will follow the LME trend if LME copper can maintain its upward trend in the short term," he added.
Traders said they expected copper to rise steadily in the next few days.
Physical prices are around 23,600 yuan per tonne in the Shanghai area, traders said.
Aluminium ended up in slow trading. May rose 100 to 15,550, June 60 to 15,810 and July 50 to 15,960.
Combined volume fell to 740 tonnes from 1,480.
